chapter_title: Paul at Ephesus, Part 2: Ideas, Legacy, and Lessons in Leading Change
learning_objective: The learner will judge whether each of twelve school practices is an essential purpose of schooling or an inherited form that served that purpose under earlier constraints, judging at least 10 of 12 correctly, including both items of the trap pair.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** essential-or-inherited-school-practices
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Evaluate
**Bloom Verb:** judge
**Learning Objective:** The learner will judge whether each of twelve school practices is an essential purpose of schooling or an inherited form that served that purpose under earlier constraints, judging at least 10 of 12 correctly, including both items of the trap pair. **Prerequisites:** essential versus inherited, the Council of Jerusalem, the grammar of schooling, seat time, the Carnegie unit, direct instruction, the AI-native school (all defined in the chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each of 12 practice cards, the learner chooses Essential or Inherited before feedback appears. A choice is correct when it matches the "Correct judgment" column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt, including cards 5 and 11, the trap pair. **Misconceptions:** (1) Inherited means worthless or harmful; in fact inherited forms solved real problems and may still be useful. (2) Whatever schools have always done must be essential. (3) Checking that a student has learned (card 5) is the same as everyone taking the same test on the same day (card 11). (4) Explanation by a teacher is inherited; what is inherited is the single pace for the whole room (card 10). **Instructional Rationale:** Judging each practice against a stated criterion is an Evaluate task. The criterion, the chapter's test "What problem did this solve, and does that problem still exist in the same form?", is shown on every card, and the trap pair forces the learner to separate a purpose from the form that once carried it. **Content:** The criterion shown at the top: "Essential: part of what a school is for. Inherited: one way of doing it that answered the constraints of an earlier age." Cards, in this fixed order: | # | Practice shown to the learner | Correct judgment | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | Every student learns to read, write, and reason with numbers. | Essential | This is the academic core a school exists to teach. | | 2 | A high school credit equals about 120 hours of class time. | Inherited | The Carnegie unit was defined in 1906 to standardize transcripts and pensions; it measures hours, not learning. | | 3 | Students get timely, specific feedback on their practice. | Essential | Feedback is how practice turns into learning, whatever the method. | | 4 | Students are grouped into grades by birth year. | Inherited | Age grading spread in the 19th century to move many children through a building; it sorts by age, not readiness. | | 5 | Someone checks that a student has really learned a skill before building on it. (trap) | Essential | Checking mastery is part of teaching; only the way and the timing of the check are matters of form. | | 6 | A bell moves every student to a new subject about every 50 minutes. | Inherited | The period schedule coordinates a large building; it is one way to divide time, not a purpose. | | 7 | Each student is known well by at least one caring adult. | Essential | Relationships with adults are part of what a school is for, and AI does not replace them. | | 8 | Students sit in rows facing the teacher. | Inherited | Rows suit one person explaining to many; other arrangements suit other ways of learning. | | 9 | Students practice working, talking, and disagreeing well with other people. | Essential | Learning with others is a core purpose; it is what the AI-native afternoon is for. | | 10 | New material is explained to the whole class at a single pace. | Inherited | Explanation is essential; one pace for everyone is the inherited form, which leaves many students out of reach. | | 11 | Every student takes the same unit test on the same day. (trap) | Inherited | Checking learning is essential (card 5); the shared date comes from moving a whole class together. | | 12 | Students are safe in body and mind during the school day. | Essential | Safety is a precondition of learning, and families rely on it. | Answer counts: Essential 6, Inherited 6. Trap pair: cards 5 and 11. **Provenance:** Cards 2, 4, 6, and 10 come from this chapter's sections "Seat Time and the Carnegie Unit," "The Grammar of Schooling," and "Direct Instruction," which follow *AI-Native Schools*, Chapters 1, 3, and 18. Cards 1, 3, 7, and 9 follow the chapter's sections "Essential Versus Inherited" and "The AI-Native School." The judgments apply the chapter's stated criterion; the sim labels the set "Judgments follow this chapter's criterion; reasonable people may weigh some forms differently." **Rules:** - Each card has exactly one correct judgment, given in Content. - One scored attempt per card; the first choice is the one scored. - Score is the number of first-attempt correct choices, 0 to 12. - Mastery is score >= 10 with cards 5 and 11 both correct. - Cards appear one at a time in the fixed order. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the criterion. 2. For each card, the learner chooses Essential or Inherited. 3. Feedback appears, and the card joins one of two growing columns, Essential or Inherited, marked correct or incorrect. 4. After card 12, the learner sees both columns side by side, with cards 5 and 11 linked by a line labeled "purpose and form." 5. The learner should notice that every inherited form on the list serves an essential purpose on the list, which is why it is hard to change. **Feedback:** Twelve cards, fixed order, one scored attempt each. Correct: "Correct. [Why]" Incorrect: "This one is [correct judgment]. [Why]" If card 11 is judged Essential: add "The check is essential; the shared test date is a form." If card 10 is judged Essential: add "Keep the explanation, question the single pace." After card 12: "[n] of 12 correct." If mastery is met: "You can separate a purpose from the form that carried it." Otherwise: "Look again at cards 5 and 11: which is the purpose, and which is one way of doing it?" A "Try again" option repeats all twelve cards. **Starting State:** The criterion, two empty columns labeled Essential and Inherited, and card 1, with the question "Is this part of what a school is for, or one way of doing it?" **Chapter Anchors:** Carnegie unit defined in 1906 as 120 hours of class time; the test "What problem did this solve when it began, and does that problem still exist in the same form?"; 50-minute periods; twelve practices, six of each.
